children: G-III Apparel reported higher earnings in its fiscal second quarter, even as net sales fell and came in below expectations.

The owner of Marc Jacobs and DKNY on Wednesday posted a profit of $20.2 million, or 46 cents a share, for its three months ended July 31. That compares with a profit of $10.9 million, or 25 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out one-time items, earnings came in at 26 cents a share. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected adjusted earnings of 23 cents a share.
Net sales fell 9.6% to $554.1 million, missing Wall Street estimates for $570.4 million.

Chief Executive Morris Goldfarb attributed G-III's higher earnings largely to gross margin expansion. He added that the company's acquisition of fashion brand Marc Jacobs stands to strengthen its portfolio.
Shares fell 12%, to $28.40, in premarket trading.

For the year, G-III now expects earnings of $4.10 to $4.20 a share, and adjusted earnings of $2.20 to $2.30 a share. The company had previously guided for earnings of $3.85 to $3.95 a share, and adjusted earnings of $2.15 to $2.25 a share.

The company backed its outlook for net sales to come in around $2.71 billion. G-III said the figure includes the loss of about $460 million in sales from Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger products, after the company lost a licensing agreement it previously held for those brands.
Analysts are looking for adjusted earnings of $2.22 a share on net sales of $2.71 billion.

G-III said its outlook assumes tariffs for the remainder of the year will stay at current rates. The company also noted that its guidance doesn't include any impact related to the Marc Jacobs acquisition, which is expected to be slightly dilutive in its fiscal 2027. G-III said it will provide more specific guidance during third-quarter earnings.
